messages:
ops-bot: [ALERT] Hosted API p95/p99 spike detected in us-west2 starting at 2024-11-05T14:21:40Z (ts 3359876500). p95 jumped from ~120ms to 850ms, p99 to ~2.1s. Grafana: <https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/hosted/api-latency>
maya: seeing it on dashboards too. Router queue depth hit ~1.8k (norm ~100-200). Tail latency aligns with queue bump.
dmitri: any deploys in last 30m? checking CI/deploy-bot now.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: no prod deploys in last 2h. No config pushes recorded in last 3h.
liam: kernel-selector logs show increased fallback_kernel usage starting ~14:19 UTC. fallback_kernel invocation count +400%.
maya: KV cache hit-rate for us-west2 dropped from 92% -> 48% around 14:18. Eviction rate spiked. Looks like prefix churn.
soumaya: rateengine: earlier today we relaxed tenant burst (PR #1423) for onboarding. I'm worried a noisy tenant is now able to fanout bursts.
dmitri: can we correlate high-fanout tenant traces from router? running query to pull trace ids: ```
curl -sS "https://router-api/internal/traces?region=us-west2&since=3359876400&tag=kernel_selector=fallback" | jq '.[] | {ts, tenant, seq_len, kernel}' | head
```
ops-bot: trace query returned many entries for tenant "t-42"; seq_len distribution: 512, 2048, 8192 (heavy tail).
liam: t-42 is sending a lot of long-context requests (seq_len ~8k). That explains kernel-selector choosing aux_slow kernel for memory reasons.
maya: long sequences + KV cache miss amplification -> memory pressure -> batching sampler reduces batch sizes -> more per-request overhead -> higher p95. Kernel mispick amplifies per-token time.
liam: GPU util not saturated, but memory allocation churn high and kernel exec time per token increased ~3x for aux_slow vs primary_kernel.
natalie: proposed mitigation plan: (1) immediately throttle tenant t-42 fanout (rateengine) -> ops (2) temporarily prefer primary_kernel for seq_len < 8192 via kernel-selector config override -> eng (3) pin hot prefixes in KV cache to prevent eviction thrash -> eng-ops (4) follow up with postmortem and revert PR #1423 if needed.
soumaya: applied emergency ratecap rule: tenant t-42 -> 50 rps. Watching.
ops-bot: rateengine: rule applied, throttle in effect. Rejected reqs from t-42 down 95%.
maya: after throttle, router queue depth dropped from 1.8k -> 200 in ~90s. p95 back to ~150ms, p99 trending down.
dmitri: rolling kernel-selector heuristic rollback now (revert PR link: https://git.internal/revert/ks-heuristic). Planning canary in 10m.
liam: applying KV cache protection: pin top-100 prefixes for us-west2; running patch now.
natalie: good. Owners: soumaya -> ops ratecap and monitor; dmitri -> kernel-selector rollback + canary; liam/maya -> KV pin + validate batch sampler; natalie -> coordinate postmortem and assign follow-ups.
maya: quick profiling snippet that helped identify the mispick: ```
# from perf dump
timestamp 14:18:32 kernel=aux_slow seq_len=8192 tokens=1024 exec_us=41000 kv_miss=true batching_size=1
timestamp 14:18:45 kernel=primary seq_len=256 tokens=1024 exec_us=12000 kv_miss=false batching_size=16
```
dmitri: root cause hypothesis: relaxed burst rules + a single noisy tenant sending long-context fanout requests caused KV cache churn and forced kernel-selector to pick a memory-conservative but slower kernel; combined with reduced batching under memory pressure -> latency spike.
soumaya: monitoring: p95 back near baseline. Keeping ratecap for 30m then reassess.
liam: will also add a guard in kernel-selector: if fallback_kernel latency > X for same seq_len distribution, prefer primary until memory pressure is resolved.
natalie: opened incident ticket INC-2024-442 and scheduled postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 PT. Add data dumps and traces to the ticket.
maya: thanks all. Marking thread for follow-ups: please drop short notes to the incident ticket with timelines and PRs.
ops-bot: [NOTE] If p95/p99 re-spikes, alert channel #incidents and ping @oncall immediately :rotating_light:
natalie: closing this thread for now, moving to incident ticket. Great quick response. :thumbsup:
